audit.why: Content win and full phases[].side are identical — Skill / Vayne / Vayne / Skill / Skill / Vayne / Vayne — and that matches Trundle losing at 48.83% over 342 games. No chart edit needed; the difficulty rating (7/10) and report[14] agree with it too.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] puts Vayne's true-damage spike at first item: "Vayne's first Kraken Slayer activates percent-max-HP true damage on her third hit". Final Hour is absent from the whole page — spikes, wants, early, mid, late, whys, breakdown, dosFull, dontsFull and report never name it.
audit.why: Silver Bolts is her W, not an item. The third consecutive attack or ability on the same target has been percent-max-health true damage since she learned the spell, so a player waiting for Kraken Slayer to fear it has already lost four levels of trades. And her level-6 spike is real: Final Hour gives bonus Attack Damage, a shorter Tumble cooldown, more Night Hunter move speed and Invisibility during every Tumble — which breaks target lock mid-chase. The page describes level 6 entirely in terms of Trundle's ultimate and never mentions hers.
audit.corrected: Silver Bolts is live from level 2; Kraken Slayer only adds to a percentage she has had all lane. Level 6 is Final Hour: bonus AD, faster Tumble, invisible Tumbles.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[1] tells the Vayne to "Condemn you into a wall when Pillar of Ice is down", and every other Pillar line on the page treats the pillar as pure upside.
audit.why: This is exactly inverted, and it is the most important interaction in the matchup. Condemn knocks back and stuns on collision with terrain. Pillar of Ice creates impassable terrain. A Trundle who drops the pillar between himself and Vayne has just handed her a wall in the middle of an open lane, on her terms, at 550 range. The pillar has to go behind her, sealing a retreat that Night Hunter never speeds up — Riot's text gives her move speed only when moving toward enemy champions.
audit.corrected: Condemn stuns on any terrain, including the Pillar of Ice you just placed. Pillar behind her, never between you.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] says Vayne should "Tumble sideways on every Chomp attempt so Silver Bolts stacks reset", and whys[2] says Pillar cuts "the diagonal Tumble she relies on to reset Silver Bolts stacks".
audit.why: Tumble does not reset her own stacks — it is her auto-attack reset and it empowers the next shot, which is the burst tell _missing-interactions.json flags for this matchup. More importantly, Riot's Silver Bolts text counts "the third consecutive attack or ability against the same target", so Condemn adds a stack too. Auto, auto, Condemn is a complete round of true damage, and the page never tells the player that abilities count.
audit.corrected: Silver Bolts counts attacks and abilities alike — Condemn completes the round. Tumble is her auto-reset and her burst tell.

audit.whatIsWrong: Subjugate is described as an armour drain in four fields — spikes[1] "drains a chunk of her armor", wants.you[2] "draining her armor mid-fight", whys[4] "Subjugate's armor drain", `mid` "drain half her armor onto yourself ... the drain payoff is smaller than against Malphite".
audit.why: The steal is 40%, not half, and against Vayne the resistance half of the ability is the small half. The same cast deals 20/25/30% of her maximum health as magic damage and heals Trundle for that same amount, half of it over the following 4 seconds. On Vayne's health bar that is the trade, and the page's conclusion that R is a weak buy against a squishy is the reason a player holds it.
audit.corrected: 40% of her resists, plus a fifth of her max health as damage and the same again as healing — inside 650 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: `mid` gives the only cooldown figure on the page and it is wrong: "Track Condemn's cooldown precisely — it is around 18 seconds at level 1".
audit.why: Condemn is 20/18/16/14/12 seconds; 18 is rank 2. The whole all-in rule is built on that number, and it happens to sit almost exactly on top of Pillar of Ice at 21 seconds at rank 1 — the two answers trade one for one, which is a cleaner rule than the page manages. Tumble is 6/5/4/3/2s and drops further under Final Hour, so she gets a reset every two seconds late while Chomp stays at 3.5.
audit.corrected: Condemn 20/18/16/14/12s against Pillar of Ice 21s at rank 1 — one answer each. Tumble 6/5/4/3/2s.

audit.why: Silver Bolts is true damage, so report[8]'s Plated Steelcaps and Sterak's are about her physical autos rather than the percentage, and Doran's Shield into her poke is right. No Vayne ability carries a heal flag, so the absence of anti-heal is correct. Left alone.
The packet's suspectName "Frozen Domain's" in spikes[1] is a false positive — a possessive, not a misnaming.

edits.before: At level 1 Chomp is your entire gameplan: step up and bite her on every minion wave so the AD steal and bonus damage hit before her Silver Bolts stacks to three. She cannot out-trade you in a one- or two-hit exchange because you are sapping her own attack damage. Level 2, drop Frozen Domain immediately when she steps forward — the movement speed bonus lets you stick through her Tumble repositioning and turn what should be her escape into another Chomp. By level 3 you have Pillar of Ice to wall off her retreat: threaten the side she typically Tumbles toward, force her to burn Condemn early, and then commit your full pattern while it is on cooldown. These three levels are the window where you build a small advantage; bank it, do not blow it on a greedy all-in that lets her Condemn you into the wall.
edits.after: At level 1 Chomp is your entire gameplan: step up and bite her on every minion wave so the AD sap lands before Silver Bolts reaches its third hit. She cannot out-trade you in a one- or two-hit exchange because you are taking her own attack damage away. Level 2, drop Frozen Domain the moment she steps forward — the move speed lets you stick through Tumble and turn what should be her escape into another Chomp. By level 3 you have Pillar of Ice, and here is the trap: Condemn stuns anything it knocks into terrain, and your pillar is terrain. Put it behind her, sealing a retreat that Night Hunter never speeds up, and never between the two of you. Count her hits as well as her cooldowns — Condemn adds a Silver Bolts stack, so auto, auto, Condemn is a full round.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 5 are the delicate window: her Silver Bolts damage is real now and she will try to kite you outside Frozen Domain while stacking the true damage. Never engage without the W zone active and never let Pillar sit unused when she retreats — cut her diagonal Tumble escape paths so she has to either fight inside your domain or burn Flash. At level 6 Subjugate is the equalizer: the moment she commits to a trade, cast R to drain half her armor onto yourself, then let the W zone and Chomp AD steal do the rest. She is not a tank, so the drain payoff is smaller than against Malphite, but it still shifts the fight's math enough that she cannot freely all-in you with Condemn. Track Condemn's cooldown precisely — it is around 18 seconds at level 1 and comes down with ability haste; the moment it is on cooldown, that is your window.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 5 are the delicate window: Silver Bolts is real now and she will kite you outside Frozen Domain while rounding the third hit. Never engage without the W zone active and never let Pillar sit unused when she retreats — but put it behind her, because Condemn stuns on collision with terrain and a pillar dropped in front of you is a wall she gets for free. At level 6 both ultimates land at once. Subjugate takes 40% of her armour and MR onto you and, the part this lane forgets, a fifth of her max health as damage plus the same again as healing — on Vayne that is the entire trade. Final Hour answers with bonus AD, more Night Hunter speed, a faster Tumble and Invisibility during every Tumble. Track Condemn precisely: 20 seconds at rank 1, and the moment it is spent is your window.

edits.before: Once she completes Kraken Slayer and Guinsoo's, Silver Bolts' true damage on every third hit ignores everything you build — Frozen Domain healing helps but does not cancel percent-max-HP damage at scale. Stop dueling her 1v1 in side lanes past two items and start playing Subjugate for team fights: drain your team's tankiest frontliner if she is not in range, or wait for her to commit onto a teammate before you lock her down with Pillar and drain her armor as she tries to Tumble-kite away. You are still impactful in 5v5 objective fights because Subjugate into any tanky ally or foe is a resistance swing, but solo she wins every extended brawl at this stage.
edits.after: Once she completes Kraken Slayer and Guinsoo's, Silver Bolts' true damage on every third hit goes through everything you build — Frozen Domain healing helps but never cancels a percentage of your own health bar. You are still decisive in 5v5 objective fights because Subjugate on any tanky target is a resistance swing plus a heal, but solo she wins every extended brawl here.

notes: The headline finding is that Pillar of Ice is a liability in this matchup as often as an asset: Condemn stuns on collision with terrain and Pillar of Ice is impassable terrain, so a pillar placed between Trundle and Vayne is a free wall-stun for her. wants.foe[1] currently says the opposite — that she wants the pillar DOWN — which is the most dangerous single line on the page. Both halves come straight from Riot's own ability text in the kit library, but it is worth a human spot-check because the advice change is large. Second theme, shared with the Teemo entry: 'Subjugate is weak against squishies' is templated and wrong — the max-health damage and the equal heal make it strongest against exactly those health bars. Third: Silver Bolts counting abilities as well as attacks (so Condemn completes a round) is in Riot's text and appears on no Trundle page I read.
